summary: You have produced a well-organised report that addresses every requirement, with checkable orbit, drag and access calculations supported by STK files in Appendix A. Your conclusions are specific and quantified. Marks were reduced mainly for a few numerical inconsistencies, unjustified assumptions in the data budget and eclipse analysis, an unsourced figure, and some uncited statements. Addressing these would strengthen an already strong report.
next_steps: Reconcile the contact-time figures in Section 2.4: 510 s of 771 s is about 66%, not the 60% stated, so check the 34 minutes per day against this.

Justify the one-strip-per-day imaging assumption in Table 6 against your 14.9 orbits per day and 5-day revisit claim, cite a source for the 4:1 compression ratio, and correct the downlink time (2,000 s is 33.3 minutes, not 34).

Derive your 34-minute eclipse duration from the node time or beta angle, credit the source of Figure 2, cite the uncited claims (such as the reef-dependent value and the funding statement), and describe the lifetime estimates as order-of-magnitude because drag increases as altitude falls.

criteria.C1: You clearly address all four required items: the primary mission, why it is needed, the single-spacecraft choice and its justification, and the operator and customers. Your rationale is supported by several cited sources, including NOAA, AIMS context and fluid lensing papers. To strengthen it further, add citations to the claim about hundreds of millions relying on reefs and to your funding statement, which are currently unreferenced.
criteria.C2: Your design is comprehensive and well evidenced, covering launch on Vega C, orbit elements, manoeuvres, ground station, contact statistics, data budget and end-of-life. Your key calculations check out and are backed by STK figures and appendix files. Marks were reduced for the contact-time percentage that does not match your figures, an unjustified daily-imaging assumption, an unsourced Figure 2, and an eclipse duration that is asserted rather than derived.
criteria.C3: Your conclusions are detailed and follow from your evidence, quantifying the result that a 4 m² drag sail removes the satellite in about two years compared with about 32 years without it. You also identify four specific limitations, namely the Vega C launch risk, fluid lensing at 5 m, the missing X-band link budget and the 45-day revisit, and propose mitigations for each.
criteria.C4: Your report follows a clear engineering structure, with an executive summary, numbered sections, labelled tables and figures, and an appendix of STK files, and uses consistent IEEE-style citations. Marks were reduced for awkward phrasing (for example, 'but this is not even the full extent of their nurture' in Section 1), a contents list without page numbers, an unsourced Figure 2, and several uncited statements.
